_meta.indication: BRUKINSA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least one prior therapy, under accelerated approval based on overall response rate.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm trial; BRUKINSA 160 mg twice daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated patients with mantle cell lymphoma who had received at least one prior therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per independent review committee
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 84% (95% CI: 74, 91) per IRC; complete response 59% (95% CI: 48, 70); median duration of response 19.5 months (95% CI: 16.6, NE)

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, dose-escalation, global, multicenter, single-arm trial; BRUKINSA 160 mg twice daily or 320 mg daily
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated MCL patients (subpopulation of a B-cell malignancy trial)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per independent review committee
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 84% (95% CI: 67, 95) per IRC; complete response 22% (95% CI: 9, 40); median duration of response 18.5 months (95% CI: 12.6, NE)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): neutrophil count decreased (53%), platelet count decreased (39%), upper respiratory tract infection (38%), white blood cell count decreased (30%), hemoglobin decreased (29%), rash (25%), bruising (23%), diarrhea (20%), and cough (20%). Serious risks include hemorrhage (major hemorrhage 3%), Grade 3+ infections (30%), Grade 3/4 cytopenias, and atrial fibrillation/flutter (2%).
target_moa: Zanubrutinib is a Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor that forms a covalent bond with cysteine residue (Cys481) in the BTK active site, resulting in irreversible inactivation of the kinase; the BTK pathway is involved in the development, maintenance, and progression of B-cell malignancies.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee because zanubrutinib is not first-in-class and the application did not raise new efficacy or safety issues.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR); considered an intermediate endpoint in MCL supported by duration of response

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate [see *Clinical Studies* (14.1)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.
The use of overall response rate in mantle cell lymphoma is considered an intermediate endpoint and is clinically meaningful with supporting evidence from duration of response.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Complete and submit final results of Trial BGB-3111-306, the randomized Phase 3 trial of BRUKINSA plus rituximab versus bendamustine and rituximab in previously untreated MCL, with primary endpoint PFS by IRC.

citations.quote: PMR 3735-1 Complete and submit the final results of Trial BGB-3111-306 - the ongoing randomized, Phase 3 clinical trial of BRUKINSA in combination with rituximab versus bendamustine and rituximab in patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint is progression free survival (PFS) as assessed by Independent Review Committee (IRC). Overall survival (OS) is a key secondary endpoint. PFS and OS would be analyzed based on superiority testing. Enrollment of approximately 500 patients is expected.

summary.text: Zanubrutinib (BRUKINSA) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 for relapsed/refractory MCL based on overall response rate, with a Priority review and prior Orphan Drug Designation for mantle cell lymphoma; continued approval is contingent on a confirmatory Phase 3 trial (BGB-3111-306).

citations.quote: The review team recommends accelerated approval of zanubrutinib under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H for the indication "for treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma who have received at least one prior therapy." The recommended dose is 160mg orally twice daily or 320mg once daily.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate [see *Clinical Studies* (14.1)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.
